evidence.claim: Record 3Q26: revenue $1,235.8mn (+138% YoY), product revenue above $1bn for the first time; FY26 revenue guide raised a third time to $4.4bn-$4.6bn. Management calls 5 GW of capacity 'just a milestone' and says backlog grows faster than revenue.
evidence.numbers: Cash did not follow: operating cash flow -$27.1mn and FCF -$180.6mn as contract assets rose $430.3mn; no backlog figure; RPO $661.2mn.

evidence.claim: SpaceX reached 1.4 GW of nameplate compute at Colossus on gas generation behind the meter, guided to over 2 GW by end-2026 and 'closer to 10 GW than 5' by end-2027, and targets 15-20 GW of power and cooling so that power, not chips, is the surplus. Mobile turbines (69 units) are being replaced by a permitted 1.2 GW plant, a 900 MW Solaris joint venture and 3.3 GWh of batteries.
evidence.numbers: Known generation supports about 2 GW; sites and power for the remaining 8 GW are not public. Q2 AI capex $15.8B.
evidence.source: SpaceX Q2 2026 call; World-Energy on the Mississippi turbine agreement

evidence.claim: New wording in the 3Q26 10-Q: leases not yet commenced now include 'energy-related infrastructure', and commitments include 'energy service agreements for data centers'. Neither appeared in the 2Q26 10-Q. Meta now contracts for dedicated energy as well as halls. It does not say whether this is behind the meter.
Lined up about 11.5 GW of gas power islands for up to 10 GW of AI compute; no customer yet.
Booked more than 1 GW of behind-the-meter gas generation for one data center.
Blackstone and others committed $5.34B for 49% of Williams' behind-the-meter power projects.
Off-grid power in Texas costs about $150–200 per MWh at about $2,700 per kW with up to 2x overbuild (Brian Janous).

question: How fast are on-site and gas-to-compute builds scaling, and at what cost?
summary: On-site gas has gone mainstream: Goldman sees 67 GW behind the meter by 2030, and engine and turbine makers are sold out for years. Costs are high, about $150–200 per MWh off-grid in Texas, so it wins on speed, not price.
title: Behind-the-meter and gas-to-compute
